title: The Dove and the Ant
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, on a warm summer's day, a little ant went down to the stream for a drink of cool water.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She leaned over the edge to take a sip, when a little wave swept her right off her feet, and carried her away!

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [frightened, calling out] Help! Oh, help! I can't swim!
lines.text: Help! Oh, help! I can't swim!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: High in a tree above the stream, a gentle dove heard her tiny cry.

lines.speaker: dove
lines.speech: [calm, kind, reassuring] Hold on, little one. I'm coming!
lines.text: Hold on, little one. I'm coming!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dove plucked a leaf from the branch, and let it float down onto the water, right beside the ant.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ant climbed onto the leaf, and drifted safely to the bank, like a little boat.

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [breathless, very grateful] Thank you, kind dove! I will never forget this.
lines.text: Thank you, kind dove! I will never forget this.

lines.speaker: dove
lines.speech: [warm, gentle] You are most welcome, little friend.
lines.text: You are most welcome, little friend.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A few days later, a young fox came creeping through the meadow, with a big net in his paws.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.speech: [whispering, mischievous] What a pretty dove. I'll catch her, and keep her all for my very own.
lines.text: What a pretty dove. I'll catch her, and keep her all for my very own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dove was cooing happily in the sunshine, and did not see him tiptoeing closer, and closer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But someone else did. The little ant!

lines.speaker: ant
lines.text: Oh no you don't!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She ran as fast as her six little legs could carry her, and gave the fox a big pinch on his toe.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: Ouch! Ow, ow, ow!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fox hopped about and dropped his net, and the dove flew safely up into the sky.

lines.speaker: dove
lines.speech: [grateful, warm] Thank you, little ant. You saved me, just as I saved you.
lines.text: Thank you, little ant. You saved me, just as I saved you.

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [happy, proud] One good turn deserves another!
lines.text: One good turn deserves another!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the fox? He rubbed his toe, and decided that doves are much nicer to watch, than to catch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So remember, little one. No act of kindness is ever too small.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, the dove settled into her soft nest, high up in the tree.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And down below, the little ant curled up in her cosy home among the roots.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stream sang its quiet song, the fireflies glowed, and the stars came out, one by one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
